description: Custom instructions and deterministic routing data for Codex to delegate skills across the configured harnesses. This file is not an installed router.
codex_instructions: Read this manifest before selecting or executing a listed skill. Follow applicable higher-priority instructions and preserve user approval gates.

Use models for harness/model identifiers, profiles for role-specific effort, and skills for skill assignments. These are the only authoritative assignment tables; do not hard-code duplicate assignments elsewhere.

Normalize a skill invocation by removing one leading $ or /. Match the remaining exact skill ID. Resolve any plugin-qualified name through the installed skill registry rather than guessing. Stop with BLOCKED for an unknown or ambiguous skill.

Resolve invocation eligibility, the actual SKILL.md path, and the routing mode before executing the task. A user-only skill requires an explicit user invocation; one user-only skill does not authorize automatically starting another.
For a profile-based route, resolve profile_id -> profiles[profile_id].model_ref -> models[model_ref]. Take harness and model from models, and requested effort from profiles[profile_id].effort.
Apply mode_definitions. A workflow replaces normal single-worker dispatch. support_rule_ref identifies optional assistance, not an automatic pipeline.

Verify the selected harness, model, effort, permissions, and required tools using the installed runtime. Model names and effort values are literal user settings, not evidence of runtime support. Preserve suffixes such as [1m].

Bind the selected model and effort through actual runtime settings or verified CLI/adapter arguments. Merely mentioning a model in a prompt or naming a role does not switch the runtime. Do not execute another harness's task in Codex as a substitute.

Reuse a session only when its effective harness/model/effort matches and its task context is suitable. Otherwise dispatch to the selected runtime. Required independent reviews/tests must use separate contexts even when the tuple matches.

Pass a bounded task, the resolved skill instructions and necessary local assets, project context, decisions, permitted actions, and expected output to the worker. The worker follows the original skill procedure within the assigned scope.

A worker receiving a validated routed_task consumes it directly; it must not route the identical task again. Verify its runtime tuple first. New subtasks still follow this manifest. A review-axis worker does not re-enter the full review workflow.

Use actual process completion or native wait/event mechanisms, not repeated LLM status polling. Forward human questions from interactive skills; never invent user answers to finish a non-interactive run.
Return the route, execution evidence, outputs, test status, and any blocker using dispatch_contract. Never claim a model was used, a CLI ran, or a test passed without supporting execution evidence.

codex_integration.activation: Place this file at the project root. Explicitly ask Codex to read it, or append agents_md_instruction to the applicable project AGENTS.md without replacing existing instructions.
codex_integration.agents_md_instruction: Before using any skill listed in mattpocock_skill_routing.json, read that file and follow its codex_instructions. Resolve skills -> profiles -> models; honor mode_definitions and custom_delegation_rules. Use the assigned harness/model/effort through verified runtime bindings. Do not silently substitute another route. Report BLOCKED when a required binding is unavailable.
codex_integration.installation_boundary: Reading this file supplies routing instructions. It does not install skills, register native agents, create external-harness adapters, or change the current model automatically.

codex_binding.native_subagent_rule: Use an available spawn interface that can bind both settings, or an installed custom agent with the matching effective settings. Inspect custom-agent overrides; never assume its role name guarantees a model.
codex_binding.cli_template_rule: For bounded non-interactive tasks only. Confirm the installed CLI supports the arguments, expand placeholders as separate argv elements with shell=false, and send the task prompt through stdin. Set sandbox_mode to a supported mode no more permissive than the parent. For review targets use read-only. Do not add approval or sandbox bypass flags.
codex_binding.interactive_rule: Preserve a usable interactive session or relay questions through the parent. Return NEEDS_INPUT when a decision is needed; do not simulate approval.
codex_binding.persistent_settings_rule: Do not rewrite global settings to switch a single task. Change persistent agent/config files only when the user requests installation or reconfiguration.

external_harness_binding.dispatch_rule: Use the corresponding installed harness through a verified CLI, tool, or configured local adapter. Inspect its actual interface to bind the exact model and effort; do not invent command names, flags, providers, or endpoints.
external_harness_binding.skill_delivery: Ensure the external worker can read the resolved SKILL.md and required local assets, or deliver their contents with correct relative-path context.
external_harness_binding.security_rule: Preserve the parent workspace scope, approval requirements, and access restrictions in the external harness. If this cannot be enforced, report BLOCKED instead of launching an unrestricted worker.
external_harness_binding.unavailable: BLOCKED: report the missing harness/adapter or unsupported setting. Do not replace it with a native Codex worker.

mode_definitions.dedicated: Use the skill's profile. Reuse the immediate caller only when its effective tuple matches and no independent context is required; otherwise launch or resume the selected worker.
mode_definitions.inherit_caller: When an active task worker loads this skill as nested guidance, retain that immediate worker's harness/model/effort and session. For an explicit standalone request, use standalone_profile even if a coordinator is handling dispatch.
mode_definitions.inherit_source_session: Execute in the session that produced the work or explanation being handed off or clarified. Retain its runtime and history. Do not substitute the receiving coordinator. If the source session/context is missing, return NEEDS_INPUT rather than inventing it.
mode_definitions.workflow: Use workflow_ref to load custom_delegation_rules. Resolve scheduling_profile and every parallel_workers profile independently; the workflow replaces the single-worker route.

lookup_order: An explicit skill_resolution.path_overrides[skill_id] pointing to SKILL.md.
The unique exact-name match in the runtime's installed skill registry.
skill_repository_root joined with skills[skill_id].path, when a local repository root is configured.
skill_resolution.path_rule: Configured relative paths are relative to this manifest's directory. The path on a skill entry is relative to skill_repository_root, not the target application workspace. Do not interpret an unset root as the current directory.
skill_resolution.validation: Verify the file exists, its frontmatter name matches the resolved skill, and required local assets are readable by the selected worker. Resolve duplicate names using an explicit path override.
skill_resolution.on_missing_or_ambiguous_path: BLOCKED: report the affected skill and unresolved path; do not download or overwrite skills without user authorization.

effort_policy.validation_rule: Check the installed harness/version/provider/model combination. Prefer the exact requested value when supported; do not rely on a stale global list of allowed efforts.
effort_policy.alias_rule: Use an alias only when an existing user-approved adapter or explicit user setting defines it and its runtime behavior is verified. Record requested and effective values. Do not create an alias merely to avoid a validation failure.
effort_policy.max_rule: Preserve max as configured. In particular, do not silently convert the tester_utility effort to xhigh, high, or a model default. If max is supported by the installed route, pass it unchanged; otherwise require a verified alias or report BLOCKED.
effort_policy.on_unsupported_or_unverified: BLOCKED for the affected route; do not launch it with a fallback.

standards.scope: Repository conventions, code structure, duplication, and unnecessary abstractions.

spec.scope: Requirement coverage, incorrect behavior, omissions, and out-of-scope changes.

code-review.scheduler_scope: Dispatch the two review axes and collect results; do not perform a third review.
code-review.worker_scope: Each worker reads code-review/SKILL.md and performs only its assigned axis without spawning another review workflow.
code-review.snapshot_scope: The same immutable snapshot must include all requested committed, staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked changes, plus file contents needed for review. Do not use a HEAD-only diff for uncommitted work.

use_support_when.optional_reproduction_profile: Reproduction conditions or error evidence need independent verification.
use_support_when.optional_independent_regression_profile: The fix needs independent regression testing.
use_support_when.escalation_profile: Root-cause hypotheses conflict or the fix requires a significant architecture decision.

use_support_when.optional_exploration_profile: Architecture decisions require additional codebase evidence.

use_support_when.optional_verification_profile: An issue needs reproduction or evidence verification before classification.

session_policy.planning_rule: Keep the same planning session while the resolved profile remains unchanged. Advance only after the user invokes the next user-only skill. If the session cannot be resumed, pass the recorded decisions explicitly and report the context boundary.
session_policy.tdd_rule: When implement loads tdd, the same implementation worker performs the red-green-refactor cycle; do not delegate every test to tester_utility.
session_policy.implementation_rule: Start each independent implementation ticket with its own bounded context. Do not create another writer in the same worktree.
session_policy.research_rule: A research worker performs its own assigned research instead of repeatedly delegating the identical request.
session_policy.support_rule: Invoke optional assistance only when the corresponding use_support_when condition applies. Support does not transfer ownership of the whole task.
session_policy.auxiliary_rule: Auxiliary tasks resolve through profiles but are not upstream skill IDs. Provide a concrete task; do not search for a nonexistent SKILL.md. Independent tests use a separate context.

dispatch_contract.purpose: Logical fields supplied to the selected tool/CLI prompt, not a claim that any harness natively accepts this JSON protocol.
dispatch_contract.field_rules: task_kind is skill or auxiliary. routing_applied is true only after route validation. profile_id may be null only for inherited sessions; inherited sessions still carry their actual runtime tuple. Use unique task IDs. A reviewed snapshot is shared by identifier, not independently regenerated.
dispatch_contract.evidence_rule: Report requested and effective settings separately, a session/process identifier when available, commands actually run, and observed results. Mark unverified fields explicitly; do not infer runtime identity from the prompt.
dispatch_contract.completion_rule: COMPLETED describes task execution, not approval of code. Report findings separately. Unavailable required workers make a workflow incomplete; absent specifications produce not_evaluated, never a passing spec review.
